nodes.summary: For a real number $a$, this is the set of points $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $0 \le x \le 1$ and $0 \le y < a$.
nodes.title: Fundamental domain of the Moebius band

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a real number, let $S = [0, 1] \times \mathbb{R}$ be the unit strip and let $f : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3$. Then $f$ is a Moebius embedding of aspect ratio $a$ if $f(1 - x, y + a) = f(x, y)$ for every $(x, y) \in S$, $f$ is $C^\infty$ on $S$, at every point of $S$ the derivative of $f$ within $S$ is a linear isometry $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3$, and $f$ is injective on $[0, 1] \times [0, a)$.
nodes.title: Moebius embedding

nodes.summary: For a real number $a$, this is the map $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ given by $(x, y) \mapsto (1 - x, y + a)$.
nodes.title: Gluing map of the Moebius band

nodes.summary: Let $a > 0$. If $f : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is a Moebius embedding of aspect ratio $a$, then $a > \sqrt{3}$. That is, a smooth embedded paper Moebius band has aspect ratio greater than $\sqrt{3}$.
nodes.title: Schwartz's optimal paper Moebius band theorem

nodes.summary: The unit strip is the set of points $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $0 \le x \le 1$, that is, $[0, 1] \times \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Unit strip
